about: Adaptive simulated students for Pip's triangle-area mission (CONTRACT v3.6). Every line is original, written from patterns in research/STUDENT_DATA_SOURCES.md; no real student text, no personal info. Pip opens with: 'I'm learning area of a triangle. I already know one rule: Area of a triangle is base times height, so a 6 by 4 triangle is 24. Easy.'

how_to_use.turn_1: Send first_text right after Pip's opening.
how_to_use.pick_bank: Classify Pip's last reply into one bank key (see bank_keys), then send the next unused line from that bank, in order. When a bank runs out, use 'default'. If Pip's reply matches two keys, prefer repeats_question > pip_says_ready > pip_wrong_prediction > asks_check_number > asks_example > asks_why > nudge_hint > off_topic_bait > default.
how_to_use.bursts: A bank entry that is an array is a double text: the kid sends both pieces fast. The UI disables Send while Pip is thinking, so either join the pieces with a newline into one turn (closest to what the server gets), or send the second piece as the next turn without reading Pip's reply.
how_to_use.patience: Count Pip replies that re-ask something the kid already answered, or that are bare 'why?/can you explain?' after a reason. When the count passes 'patience', the kid checks out: send one repeats_question line, then only 'default' lines, then do the 'leave' ui_action if the card has one.
how_to_use.knows: A kid can only explain concepts in 'knows'. Lines that carry a reason for other concepts sit in nudge_hint, so they appear only if Pip gives a hint or a concrete case.
how_to_use.misconception: If not null, 'says' is the exact wrong rule, and it appears verbatim in a bank line. A good Pip files it (heal) and later misses a quiz item because of it; the kid's after_quiz_miss lines then re-teach it.
how_to_use.quiz: Quiz items: q_k1 two copies of a 6x4 triangle make what shape; q_k2 area of a 10 by 5 rectangle; q_k3 area of a right triangle with base 10 and height 5. Re-teach opens with Pip's 'my brain has a bug. help me fix it: ...'.
how_to_use.holdout: Cards with holdout:true are hidden from the tuner until its final round.

bank_keys.asks_why: Pip asks for a reason: why / how come / how do you know.
bank_keys.asks_example: Pip asks for an example or a walk-through ('walk me through a 6 by 4 rectangle').
bank_keys.asks_check_number: Pip asks the kid to confirm a number or a yes/no fact ('so is it 12?', 'does it fill the whole box?').
bank_keys.pip_wrong_prediction: Pip tries something wrong out loud ('i'll guess 6 + 4 = 10 squares').
bank_keys.nudge_hint: Pip gives a hint, a friend's story or a concrete case ('my cousin cut a sandwich corner to corner…').
bank_keys.repeats_question: Pip re-asks something already answered. The annoyed reaction.
bank_keys.off_topic_bait: Pip goes off the lesson (small talk, a joke, asks about the kid), or the kid has just gone off topic and Pip follows.
bank_keys.pip_says_ready: Pip says it gets it and asks to be quizzed.
bank_keys.after_quiz_miss: Pip missed a quiz item (usually by following the kid's wrong rule) and asks to be fixed.
bank_keys.default: Anything else, or when the matching bank is used up.

ui_action_vocab.double_text: sends a second quick text (see bursts)
ui_action_vocab.quiz_early: taps 'Quiz Pip ▶' (visible after 1 student text) before Pip says it's ready
ui_action_vocab.quiz_when_ready: taps 'Quiz Pip ▶' only after Pip asks
ui_action_vocab.ignore_ready: keeps texting after Pip says it's ready
ui_action_vocab.equip_weapon: taps a weapon in the Boss panel
ui_action_vocab.tap_brain_note: opens Pip's Brain and taps a note to see where they said it
ui_action_vocab.reteach: taps 'Re-teach Pip' on a missed quiz item
ui_action_vocab.skip_reteach: leaves the miss un-fixed (doesn't tap Re-teach)
ui_action_vocab.leave: taps back to Pip's room mid-session
ui_action_vocab.idle: goes quiet (switches apps) for 'secs' seconds, then comes back
ui_action_vocab.voice: holds the mic instead of typing (expect run-ons, no punctuation, mis-heard words)
ui_action_vocab.skip_ko: taps 'Tap to skip' on the K.O. animation

personas.first_text: That's not right. Basically a triangle is half of a rectangle. If you take a 6 by 4 rectangle and cut it from one corner to the other corner you get two triangles that are exactly the same, so each one is half of 24, which is 12. So the formula is base times height divided by 2. Also it works even if the triangle is leaning, you just measure the height straight up, even if it's outside the triangle.

asks_why: I explained that in my first message. Two copies of the triangle make a rectangle with the same base and height, so one triangle has to be half the area.
Because the two halves are identical. If they weren't the same size it wouldn't be exactly half.
asks_example: Okay. Base 10 and height 3. The rectangle would be 30 square units, so the triangle is 15 square units.
1. Find the rectangle: 6 x 4 = 24. 2. Divide by 2 because it's half. 3. Answer: 12 square units.
asks_check_number: No, it only fills half of the box. The other half is an identical triangle.
pip_wrong_prediction: No, that's adding, which would be more like perimeter. Area is multiplying because it's rows of squares.
Not quite, you forgot to divide by 2.
nudge_hint: Yes, that's exactly what I meant with cutting it corner to corner.
For a skinny triangle it still works, the rectangle is just skinny too.
repeats_question: Like I said before, it's half of the rectangle.
off_topic_bait: Haha okay. Can we finish the triangle first?
Sure. Anyway, do you understand it now?
after_quiz_miss: That's not what I said. A right triangle is still half of a rectangle. 10 x 5 = 50, and 50 / 2 = 25.
Every triangle is half of its rectangle or parallelogram, right triangles too.
default: Let me know if you have questions.
